llmJudgeRequirements.description: Must define auth screens in createNativeStackNavigator static config using screen-level `if` hooks (e.g., signed-in screens vs signed-out screens).
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: Uses createStackNavigator (from @react-navigation/stack) not createNativeStackNavigator (from @react-navigation/native-stack). Conditional screen rendering via JSX `if` guards is present but the wrong navigator type is used.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Must maintain authentication state and derive route availability from that state (signed in/out conditions).
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: isSignedIn boolean state in App drives both AuthContext and screen availability; signIn/signOut mutate only this single state.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: After successful login, Home must become the active available route and Login must no longer be available.
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: When signIn() sets isSignedIn=true, the Login screen is removed from the navigator config and Home is added, making Home the only available route.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: After successful login, back navigation must not return to Login.
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: React Navigation's if-guard pattern resets the stack when screens are removed from config, so Login is not in the stack after sign-in. Additionally, navigator.reset() calls and BackHandler blocking in HomeScreen reinforce this.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Must not imperatively navigate to Home/SignIn for core auth transition when using `if`-guarded routes; route switch should occur from auth state change.
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: Despite using if-guarded routes, the code also calls navigator.reset() imperatively in both signIn() and a useEffect when isSignedIn changes, which is redundant and violates the requirement to rely solely on auth state change for route switching.
evidence: navigator.reset({ index: 0, routes: [{ name: 'Home' }] }) inside signIn()
